successors.text: Massalia and its territory (25 km disc round Marseille, about 1,000 km2)

ledger.x: c. 600: Phocaean Greeks found Massalia. Infobox 'Founded by Greeks from Phocaea: c. 600 BC'; 'Massalia was established c. 600 BC by Ionian Greek settlers from Phocaea, in Western Anatolia'. The History page adds the Carthaginian opposition to the project ('whose fleet was defeated'). The disc of territory is the…
Antipolis and Nikaia founded 'c. mid-3rd c.' on the coast of Gallia Narbonensis; the modern places (Antibes, Nice) are the usual identifications.
49: Caesar's siege strips Massalia of its holdings.

wars.name: Siege of Massilia
wars.outcome: The city was besieged from April 49 and fell by September to Caesar's army; it kept nominal autonomy but lost its trading empire.

wars.name: Allobroges and Arverni invasion (123 BC)
wars.outcome: 'In 123 BC, Massalia was faced by an invasion of the Allobroges and Arverni under Bituitus'; Massalia yielded 'a strip of land through its territory which was used to construct the Via Domitia' and 'the Romans organized their province of Transalpine Gaul…

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier of Massalia; its holdings are a city and coastal colonies.
